Google raises Pixel 10a price to $599 as memory costs climb
data.description:
Google (GOOG) has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a smartphone by $100 to $599 for the 128GB model, another sign of how rising memory costs are pushing up prices across the consumer electronics industry.

The Pixel 10a launched in March at $499 for the 128GB model and $599 for the 256GB version. Google’s (GOOG) U.S. website now lists the phones at $599 and $699, respectively. The price increase was first spotted on Google’s (GOOG) online store in Japan and later appeared on its U.S. website, according to 9to5Google.

The increase comes amid a persistent memory-chip shortage that has pushed up costs across the consumer electronics industry. Samsung this week raised prices on most of its Galaxy S26 smartphones by $100, while Apple (AAPL) raised prices on its iPhone 18 lineup and also increased prices on some older models.

Apple (AAPL) also departed from its usual practice of cutting prices on older iPhone models when new versions launch. Instead, the company raised prices on some older iPhones in September while also increasing prices for its new iPhone 18 Pro lineup. The year-old iPhone 17, which typically would have received a $100 price cut, instead rose by $100 to $899.

Google (GOOG) had already raised prices across its Pixel 11 lineup by $100 when it introduced the phones in August, according to Bloomberg. The company offset some of the higher starting prices by including more storage in the base configurations.

The Pixel 10a had been discounted to $424 last month. Walmart still appeared to be selling the phone for $499, although supplies were limited.

data.title: Treasury yields reverse higher after an earlier retreat against payrolls data
data.description:
U.S. Treasury yields reversed course and pushed higher after slipping across the curve Friday morning after a softer-than-expected September jobs report reinforced the view that hiring is cooling faster than economists had anticipated.

Nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 last month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said, well short of the 85,000 gain forecasted by economists. The prior month was also marked down, to 133,000 from an initially reported 162,000, extending a stretch of weaker employment readings that has already shaped expectations for Federal Reserve policy. 

The miss drew buyers into the Treasury market and pushed yields lower. However, since early trading, yields have since advanced. The rate-sensitive U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) was up 4 basis points to 4.83%. The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) advanced by 3 basis points, to 5.27%, while the longer-end U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) gained 2 basis points to 5.62%. 

The payrolls report lands as traders weigh whether a slower pace of hiring is enough to keep the Fed away from a hiking path, or whether lingering price pressures will limit how far yields can fall. Friday’s price action shows bonds treating the downside surprise as fresh evidence that the labor market is no longer running as hot as earlier estimates implied but has since crossed back to its ongoing advance.

data.title: Edison International cut to Sell equivalent at Jefferies as Eaton Fire liability set to intensify
data.description:
Edison International (EIX) down 0.9% in Friday's trading as Jefferies downgraded the utility to Underperform from Hold with a $42 price target, down from $53, saying the probability of a California legislature special session is slim and Eaton fire liabilities are not priced in.

Jefferies analysts led by Paul Zimbardo said the fundamental catalyst path ahead for Edison (EIX) skews more cautious, with a remote probability of a meaningful 2026 California legislative session outcome and Eaton Fire liabilities coming into sharper focus over the coming months, as possible criminal charges represent a near-term risk.

The Los Angeles County District Attorney said on September 23 that the criminal investigation into Southern California Edison (EIX) for the Eaton Fire is "very active," and if criminal charges are pursued, it could lead to investors pricing in higher Eaton liabilities, Zimbardo wrote.

Without the benefit of a special session, the focus of 2027 will be on the magnitude of Eaton liabilities, the analyst said, seeing Edison's (EIX) 6.5% dividend yield as safe, "but investors are closely watching."

Edison (EIX) currently trades at a significant premium to close peer PG&E (PCG), and Zimbardo said he expects the valuation spread to narrow with the crystallizing of Eaton Fire liability exposure as the core driver of investor sentiment in the upcoming months.

data.title: Whopper momentum and refranchising efforts could boost Burger King's profile with investors
data.description:
Restaurant Brands International (QSR) plans to accelerate its plan to refranchise Burger King restaurants in the U.S., shifting company-operated locations to smaller, local owner-operators. The company now expects to sell roughly 200 restaurants by the end of this year, which is below its earlier target of about 300. The restaurant operator is looking to find the right long-term operators rather than complete transactions quickly. 

The longer-term objective is to retain only about 300 company-owned stores, using them primarily for testing and training while franchisees run most of the system. The upshot for investors is that refranchising generates cash and moves Burger King toward an asset-light model, which generally carries less restaurant-level cost and can support higher corporate profitability. Just as important, Restaurant Brands (QSR) believes hands-on local franchisees can operate restaurants better because their returns are directly tied to local sales, staffing, service, and guest satisfaction.

Notably, Burger King’s U.S. sales momentum has improved sharply in 2026. Comparable sales grew 5.8% in the first quarter and accelerated to 8.5% in the second quarter. The improvement reflects the multi-year "Reclaim the Flame turnaround" and is indicative that the new refreshed Whopper is boosting traffic. Remodels also appear to be adding to the brand's recovery as full remodel locations have produced an average 11.9% sales lift.

data.title: Court overturns $22.7M patent infringement award against Gogo - update
data.description:
Updated 12:30 ET with a statement from SmartSky.

A U.S. district court in Delaware overturned a jury decision to award $22.7M to the plaintiffs in a case against Gogo Inc. (GOGO), ruling that SmartSky Networks failed to present sufficient evidence that it suffered legally recoverable damages and the amount of the award was unsupported by the actual facts.

SmartSky sued Gogo (GOGO) for patent infringement in February 2022, claiming Gogo’s (GOGO) 5G air-to-ground inflight connectivity service illegally used SmartSky’s proprietary technology. In November 2025, a jury agreed with SmartSky that Gogo (GOGO) infringed on its four patented technologies, but the $22.7M monetary award was set aside because SmartSky failed to legally prove its calculated damages. 

Although the decision is subject to appeal, Gogo (GOGO) applauded the court’s decision regarding the award and reflected on the outcome of the ruling, which represents a “significant step in resolving this matter.”

“In reaching that decision, the court found that SmartSky’s damages award was untethered to the evidentiary record, relying on assumptions that could not be reconciled with the facts of the case,” Gogo said in a statement.

In response to the court's ruling, SmartSky issued the following statement: "The most important takeaway from this opinion is that the court upheld the jury's findings that Gogo willfully infringed SmartSky's valid patents. The court found that the evidence supports the jury's conclusion that Gogo knew about SmartSky's patents and deliberately or intentionally infringed them. SmartSky is disappointed with the court's damages ruling and is evaluating its options for further relief."

data.title: Warner Bros. studio execs to leave after Paramount merger -- Variety
data.description:
Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy will reportedly step down as co-heads of Warner Bros. Pictures (WBD) once the studio merges with Paramount Skydance (PSKY) this month.

According to sources cited by Variety, De Luca and Abdy, the team behind "Sinners," "One Battle After Another," "Weapons," and the upcoming “Dune: Part 3,” will not be a part of a merged Paramount/Warner Bros. executive team. Instead, Paramount Pictures co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will run the merged Paramount Warner Bros. Motion Picture unit.

The decision to leave De Luca and Abdy out of the new Skydance comes shortly after the pair extended their Warner Bros. contracts through 2030.

The merger of Paramount Skydance (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) will be completed October 6, at which time the new company will be renamed Skydance. Former Mattel (MAT) CEO Ynon Kreiz will lead the new company along with current CEO David Ellison.
